title: Sheafification units on intersection-product presheaf terms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$, and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. For every $p\in\mathbb N$, the unit of module sheafification on the explicit presheaf term $\prod_{t:\operatorname{Fin}(p+1)\hookrightarrow_o\operatorname{Fin}(r)}(V\mapsto G(V\cap W_t))$ [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction] is an isomorphism of module presheaves. No covering or affineness assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 02FU (cohomology-lemma-covering-resolution), with the increasing-tuple convention of Tag 01FM

proof.text:
For a fixed intersection W, the presheaf V ↦ G(V intersect W) is the
direct image along the inclusion W into X of the restriction of G to W.
The scalar restriction in cechCapModule agrees with the scalar structure
of that direct image. It is therefore a sheaf. Products of these sheaves
are computed as products of presheaves, and the explicit terms are exactly
those finite products. The sheafification unit of an already sheaf
presheaf is an isomorphism, also in the category of module presheaves,
since the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. The empty product is
the zero module presheaf and is a sheaf as well.
